explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a content-only “algorithm tutorial” repository: a comprehensive LeetCode brushing guide with Markdown files organized by topic, image assets, a README, and a simple shell helper.  
   - It is not a true “app” or microservice suite but a static-site content project, intended to be published online (programmercarl.com, GitHub Pages, Gitee mirror).

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top level:  
     • README.md – overview and publish instructions  
     • pics/ – images used by the site  
     • problems/ – all Markdown tutorials organized by topic folders  
     • toolgithub.sh – a deployment helper script  
   - No backend code, no database files, no server frameworks—pure static content.

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Describes multiple publishing endpoints (programmercarl.com, Gitee, GitHub Pages).  
   - Mentions PDF, video, and contributor workflow via pull requests.

4. Main components for the system design diagram  
   a. Content authoring environment  
      - Developer workstation  
      - Git (local commits, branches)  
   b. Source repository hosting  
      - GitHub (primary)  
      - Gitee (mirror)  
   c. CI/CD pipeline  
      - GitHub Actions (or custom CI) triggered on push/PR  
      - toolgithub.sh script for build/deploy  
   d. Static site generator  
      - Hugo/Hexo/Custom scripts converting Markdown → HTML/CSS/JS  
   e. Hosting & delivery  
      - GitHub Pages & Gitee Pages or an S3/OSS bucket + CDN  
      - DNS and SSL termination  
      - CDN (for pics/, HTML, JSON)  
   f. End users  
      - Browser clients fetching from CDN/Pages endpoints  
      - Optional PDF/video hosting endpoints  

5. Relationships & interactions  
   - Developer pushes Markdown → GitHub repo  
   - CI/CD pulls changes → runs generator → outputs HTML  
   - Deployment agent pushes site to Pages branches or cloud storage  
   - CDN pulls new static assets from origin → caches globally  
   - User browser requests URL → DNS → CDN → serves cached HTML/assets  
   - Fallback mirror on Gitee for regionally reliable access  

6. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - GitOps: treat content and infrastructure as code, automatic deploy on commit  
   - Static-site hosting: no runtime servers, high cacheability, low attack surface  
   - Multisite replication: primary + mirror for availability in different regions  
   - CDN layer for performance and bandwidth offload  

7. Relevant technologies & frameworks  
   - Git, GitHub, Gitee  
   - GitHub Actions or Travis CI (CI/CD)  
   - Static-site generator (Hugo, Hexo, or custom)  
   - Hosting: GitHub Pages, Gitee Pages, or cloud storage buckets (AWS S3/Ali OSS)  
   - CDN: Cloudflare/Alibaba CDN  
   - DNS: Route53/AliDNS  
   - SSL: Let’s Encrypt or managed certificate  

8. Tailoring the diagram to this static-site project  
   - Emphasize the separation between “authoring” (Markdown author → Git) and “publishing” (CI/CD → Pages/CDN)  
   - Show two parallel publishing targets: GitHub Pages & Gitee mirror  
   - Highlight that content is purely static – no database or server runtime  

9. Diagram-drawing guidelines  
   - Use rectangles for components (GitHub, CI runner, CDN, Browser)  
   - Use directional arrows to indicate flow (author → repo → CI → hosting → CDN → users)  
   - Color-code by component type:  
     • Green for developer tools (Git, editor)  
     • Blue for hosting/CDN  
     • Orange for CI/CD  
     • Grey for static site generator  
   - Label each arrow with the action (push, build, deploy, fetch)  
   - Group components into swimlanes: Authoring, CI/CD, Hosting, Delivery, Consumption  

10. Capture essential elements without over-segmentation  
    - Don’t attempt to show every Markdown file; instead group “problems/” as “Content repository”  
    - Show the key automation steps that transform content into a live website  
    - Include a note that images under pics/ are uploaded to CDN as part of deploy  

By following these steps and focusing on the flow from Markdown → CI/CD → static hosting → CDN → end users, you will produce a clear, accurate system diagram tailored to this project’s purpose as a static algorithm tutorial website.  
</explanation>
